      Code Review

      Overall this is a solid PR with good test coverage and meaningful improvements. A few things to address:

      Bug Risk: Base64.getDecoder() vs Base64.getUrlDecoder()

      In UrlCleanupUtil.decodeBase64Url(), the standard decoder is used:

      val decoded = String(Base64.getDecoder().decode(base64Payload), UTF_8)

      Bing's redirect URLs use URL-safe Base64 (RFC 4648 §5), where + is replaced with - and / is replaced with _. The standard decoder will throw IllegalArgumentException for payloads containing those characters — which means the /aclick path is silently swallowed via catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) for any ad redirect whose destination URL contains those characters.

      Use Base64.getUrlDecoder() instead, which handles both encodings:

      val decoded = String(Base64.getUrlDecoder().decode(base64Payload), UTF_8)

      Yahoo Redirect: Embedded Tracking Params Won't Be Stripped

      extractYahooRedirectUrl returns the raw RU= segment value, which is still percent-encoded (e.g. https%3a%2f%2f...). Since StripTrackingParametersStep runs before UrlDecodingStep in the pipeline, the embedded tracking params in Yahoo-redirected URLs will never be stripped — Uri.parse() on a percent-encoded-scheme URL fails to recognize it as a valid URL.

      The test cleanUrl unwraps Yahoo redirect and then strips embedded UTM parameters actually confirms this limitation (result.stats.stripTrackingParameters asserts isFalse()) but the test name says the opposite. This should be renamed to reflect the known limitation, e.g.:

      `cleanUrl unwraps Yahoo redirect but embedded UTM parameters are not stripped (URL still encoded)`

      If stripping embedded params from Yahoo redirects is desired, extractYahooRedirectUrl should URL-decode the extracted value before returning it.

      Minor: steps Property Is Redundant Indirection

      In LinkProcessingPipeline.kt:

      class LinkProcessingPipeline(private val configuredSteps: List<LinkProcessingStep>) {
  val steps: List<LinkProcessingStep>
    get() = configuredSteps

      This is just private val configuredSteps exposed via a trivial property. It would be cleaner to make the constructor parameter directly public:

      class LinkProcessingPipeline(val steps: List<LinkProcessingStep>)

      Minor: @Immutable on StepsByPhaseMap with Mutable Map

      @Immutable
internal data class StepsByPhaseMap(
    val items: Map<ProcessingPhase, ImmutableList<LinkProcessingStep>>
)

      @Immutable is a Compose stability contract that promises the class won't mutate after construction. The Map type itself is mutable, so Compose can't verify this statically and will fall back to structural equality checks. Consider using ImmutableMap<ProcessingPhase, ImmutableList<LinkProcessingStep>> from kotlinx-collections-immutable to make the stability guarantee explicit and verifiable.

      Minor: Overly Broad Exception Catch

      In extractPathEmbeddedRedirectUrl:

      } catch (e: Exception) {
    Timber.w(e, "Failed to decode path-embedded redirect URL: $destinationUrl")
    null
}

      URLDecoder.decode only throws IllegalArgumentException. Catching Exception masks unexpected runtime errors. Prefer:

      } catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) {

      Positives

      • Step ordering fix (RemoveTrackingRedirectStep before StripTrackingParametersStep) is the right call — unwrapping redirects first lets the embedded params in destination URLs be stripped correctly. The TLDR test cases demonstrate this working end-to-end.
      • LCS-based UrlDiffHelper rewrite is a meaningful correctness improvement. The previous greedy algorithm could produce incorrect diffs when characters appeared multiple times; the DP approach is O(m×n) but URLs are short enough that this is fine.
      • defaultSteps() / fastModeSteps() refactor eliminates three separate hardcoded step lists that were getting out of sync — good DRY improvement.
      • Test coverage for the new redirect handlers is comprehensive and covers edge cases (missing params, invalid Base64, empty segments).

      Pull request overview

      This PR expands the URL-cleaning/link-processing capabilities by unwrapping additional redirect formats (Bing/Yahoo/TLDR) and adjusts pipeline configuration/UX so redirect unwrapping happens earlier and intermediate UI updates don’t show potentially-final-but-still-changing URLs.

      Changes:

      • Add redirect unwrapping support for Bing (/ck/a, /aclick), Yahoo (r.search.yahoo.com), and TLDR path-embedded redirects.
      • Refactor LinkProcessingPipeline step definitions into shared defaultSteps() / fastModeSteps() and adjust step ordering so redirect removal runs before stripping tracking params.
      • Update tests and debug tooling/UI visibility logic to reflect the new redirect handling and pipeline sequencing.

      extractYahooRedirectUrl currently returns the raw RU= segment from the encoded path (e.g., https%3A%2F%2F...). That string is not a valid URL if the user has URL-decoding disabled, so enabling “remove tracking redirect” can yield an unusable final URL. Consider percent-decoding the RU value here (and validating it starts with http/https) so redirect unwrapping always returns a usable destination URL independent of the URL-decoding preference.

            PipelineConfigurationView rebuilds defaultSteps() and re-filters them for every ProcessingPhase on each recomposition, which is unnecessary work (even if debug-only). Consider computing val allSteps = remember { LinkProcessingPipeline.defaultSteps() } once and then groupBy/associate from that, or wrapping stepsByPhase in remember so it doesn’t allocate repeatedly.
